about: The proportions of real trees, chosen per measured crown by its measurements (height, crown radius over height, the share of its surface near the apex, its photo hue) and by where the build is (a continuous plausibility cost from each entry's latitude bands, hardiness, dryness range and regional weights), so the parts a scan cannot see come from a tree of that shape that plausibly grows there. Every field the choice or the grower reads is a continuous quantity; id, label, description, sources and estimated are labels for people and prompts and nothing branches on them. A region id only joins an entry's weight to the regions table below. Read by scratchbox_tree_species.hpp.

conventions.heightM: [min, max] apex above support the form is seen at; outside it the entry costs by the log distance to the nearer bound. max: the published mature height (the larger of the sources). min: about 0.4 x the lower published mature height, a young established tree (derived, not published)
conventions.crownRadiusPerHeight: mean sector radius / height = (mean published spread / 2) / mean published height, from the sources' feet or metres; an entry whose spread is not published as a number says so under estimated
conventions.crownBaseRatio: crown base / height (0: foliage to the ground). Never published as a number: derived from the habit the sources describe (branched to the ground 0.05-0.15, low-branched 0.2-0.25, a street-tree clear trunk 0.3-0.4, a high bare trunk 0.5-0.6, a palm 0.8-0.9)
conventions.trunkRadiusPerHeight: trunk radius at the base / height. Derived from the mature trunk diameter and height the sources describe (slender 0.009-0.017, ordinary 0.018-0.025, stout 0.03-0.04); an estimate for every entry
conventions.topShare: share of the crown's surface samples within 0.35 crown radii of the apex: a hemisphere about 0.58, a 45 degree cone about 0.12, a flat top near 1. Never published: derived from the crown shape class the sources give (pyramidal or conical 0.12-0.30, columnar 0.20-0.35, upright oval 0.40-0.48, round 0.50-0.58, vase or spreading 0.60-0.70, umbrella or flat-topped 0.80-0.90)
conventions.stems: stems leaving the ground; more than one grows as a shrub
conventions.scaffoldBranches: primary limbs at the crown break (0: the grower's seeded 2-4; used for a continuous leader with whorls). Derived from the habit described, not published
conventions.leafLengthM / leafAspect: the leaf or frond the leaf set is chosen by (length, width / length), the middle of the published range; for a compound leaf, its leaflet
conventions.hueDeg: [centre, spread] of the foliage's hue in the chromaticity plane (0 red, 60 yellow, 120 green); inside the spread costs nothing. An estimate from the sources' colour words (yellow-green 85-100, mid green 105-112, dark or glossy green 115-122, blue-green needles 125-128)
conventions.apicalDominance: 0..1, the leader's dominance over the laterals: each shoot's momentum along its heading (0.76 x this) and how firmly the leader holds its course through the crown to the apex (smoothstep from 0.45 to 0.60: at 0.45 and below the trunk forks into its scaffold limbs at the crown break, from 0.60 it rises through the crown to the apex); the grower stalls on a measured crown above about 0.65 (its branches overshoot the attractors), so a columnar form is expressed by the crown's own measurements, not by a higher value. Derived from the habit described (a central leader 0.58-0.62, an oval 0.5-0.55, a rounded crown 0.38-0.45, a spreading or umbrella crown 0.25-0.35, a palm 0.2)
conventions.branchAngleRad: the laterals' angle from the leader. Derived from the habit described (fastigiate 0.25-0.3, ascending 0.5-0.7, spreading 0.8-1.0, level or drooping 1.1-1.4)
conventions.latRangesDeg: signed latitude bands [south, north] (south negative) the entry grows outdoors in; a place outside every band costs by its distance to the nearest (4 degrees costs 1). Derived from the hardiness span and the plantings the sources describe, not published; absent: uncosted. latAbsRangeDeg [min, max] is the older symmetric form and is still read
conventions.usdaZones: [coldest, warmest] published USDA hardiness zones (halves allowed: 9B is 9.5). Read as the annual extreme minimum temperature the entry lives through: zone z spans -51.1 + 5.56 (z - 1) to -51.1 + 5.56 z degrees C. A place colder than the first or with a warmer winter than the last costs by the difference (5 degrees C costs 1). The published warm limit is an eastern North American heat limit; where a species is native or common in a milder maritime winter the warm end is raised and the entry says so under estimated
conventions.aridityIndexRange: [driest, wettest] aridity index (annual precipitation / potential evapotranspiration, UNEP: below 0.05 hyper-arid, 0.05-0.2 arid, 0.2-0.5 semi-arid, 0.5-0.65 dry sub-humid, above humid) the entry grows across; outside it costs by the log distance (a factor of 2 costs 1). An estimate for every entry: the aridity classes of the regions the sources give as its range, not a published figure
conventions.regionWeights: how common the entry is in each of the regions below, 0..1 (1 native or a main street or park tree, 0.5-0.9 widely planted, 0.25-0.4 occasional); a region it does not name counts regionWeightElsewhere. The place's weight is the membership-weighted mean; it costs -ln(weight). An estimate for every entry, from the ranges and plantings the sources describe
conventions.leafRetention: the share of its foliage kept through the leafless season, 0 deciduous to 1 evergreen
conventions.leafOutMonth / leafFallMonth: months (1 = January, fractional) the leaves open and have fallen at 40 degrees north near sea level; leafPresence moves them 4 days per degree of latitude (Hopkins' bioclimatic law, 1918) and half a year south of the equator. An estimate for every entry, from the order in which the species leaf and drop in the north-eastern United States, not a published table. Not read by the grower yet
conventions.autumnHueDeg: [centre, spread] of the foliage's hue before it falls (red 5-15, orange 25-35, yellow 52-60); from the sources' autumn colour words. The photo a crown's hue was measured in may be of any season, so the match costs nothing for a hue anywhere on the arc from hueDeg to autumnHueDeg (the short way round, the spreads blended along it). Not read by the grower yet
conventions.sources: where the entry's numbers come from. Height, spread, zones and leaf size are the sources' figures (entered from the references as cited; 2026-11-05: Callery pear, zelkova, jacaranda, coconut palm, mesquite and rain tree were re-read against the references online, the rest were not re-read that day)
conventions.estimated: fields the conventions call published that are an estimate for this entry, each with how it was derived
conventions.regions: a coarse table of the world's planted regions as latitude/longitude boxes (lonDeg [west, east]; membership falls off over regionEdgeDeg past a box). minWinterTempC is the annual extreme minimum at the box's [south edge, north edge], interpolated by latitude, at referenceElevationM (above it the standard atmosphere's 6.5 degrees C per km is taken off); aridityIndex is one value for the box. Both are fits made by hand for this library to the published hardiness zones of the cities named in fitTo (USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 for the United States; the commonly cited zone of each city elsewhere) and to the UNEP aridity classes: an estimate of a place's climate from its latitude, longitude and elevation, good to about one hardiness zone, never a measurement. A caller that has a measured winter minimum or aridity index for the place passes it and the table is not used for it

entries.label: Holm oak
entries.description: A dense, rounded, very dark evergreen dome of small leathery leaves, grey beneath.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder, Quercus ilex: height, spread, hardiness zones, habit (40-70 ft by 40-70 ft, zones 7-10)
Mitchell 1974, A Field Guide to the Trees of Britain and Northern Europe (Collins), Quercus ilex: height, habit, leaf length

entries.label: Bitter (Seville) orange
entries.description: A small, compact, round evergreen head of glossy dark leaves on a short straight trunk; the street tree of southern Spain.
sources: Morton 1987, Fruits of Warm Climates, Sour Orange (Citrus aurantium): height 3-9 m, leaf 6.5-13.75 cm by 3.75-10 cm, cold tolerance
estimated: crownRadiusPerHeight: no spread published; 0.4 from the compact rounded crown described
usdaZones: from the cold tolerance described (hardier than sweet orange)

entries.label: Aleppo pine
entries.description: An open, irregular, light green crown of fine needles on a leaning or twisted trunk, rounded to flat with age.
sources: Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Pinus halepensis: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones (30-60 ft by 20-40 ft, zones 8-10)

entries.label: Jacaranda
entries.description: An open, irregular, spreading crown of fine ferny leaves on a few arching limbs; violet-blue in flower, bare briefly before it.
sources: Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Jacaranda mimosifolia: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones (ST-317: 25-40 ft by 45-60 ft, zones 9B-11)
Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder, Jacaranda mimosifolia: height, spread, hardiness zones, habit (25-50 ft by 15-30 ft)
estimated: crownRadiusPerHeight: the two sources disagree (0.81 and 0.30); 0.55 is their midpoint
leafRetention: briefly deciduous in the dry season; 0.3 is a description, not a published share

entries.label: Banyan / laurel fig
entries.description: A vast, dense, dark evergreen dome far wider than tall on a short, massive, buttressed trunk and heavy level limbs.
sources: NParks Flora & Fauna Web (Singapore), Ficus microcarpa and Ficus benghalensis: height to 30 m, leaf length

Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Ficus benghalensis, Ficus retusa: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones (zones 10B-11)
estimated: crownRadiusPerHeight: published only as "very wide"; 0.6 from the laurel fig's height and spread classes

entries.label: Mango
entries.description: A dense, dark, rounded evergreen dome of long leathery leaves on a stout short trunk.
sources: Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Mangifera indica: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones (30-45 ft by 30-40 ft, zones 10B-11)
Orwa et al. 2009, Agroforestree Database 4.0 (World Agroforestry Centre), Mangifera indica: height, crown, leaf dimensions (to 30 m)

entries.label: Royal palm
entries.description: A smooth, pale, columnar trunk with a long green crownshaft under a full head of arching feather fronds.
sources: Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Roystonea regia: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones (50-80 ft by 15-25 ft, zones 10-11)
estimated: usdaZones: warm end raised to 12.5, grown throughout the humid tropics

entries.label: Coconut palm
entries.description: A slender, curving, ringed trunk under a loose head of long yellow-green feather fronds, the lower ones drooping.
sources: Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Cocos nucifera: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones (ST-177: 50-60 ft by 15-25 ft, zones 10B-11)
Orwa et al. 2009, Agroforestree Database 4.0 (World Agroforestry Centre), Cocos nucifera: height, crown, leaf dimensions (to 30 m, fronds 4-6 m)
estimated: usdaZones: warm end raised to 13, native to equatorial coasts

entries.label: Rain tree
entries.description: A low, immense umbrella: a short stout trunk, great level limbs and a shallow dome much wider than the tree is tall.
sources: Staples & Elevitch 2006, Samanea saman (rain tree), Species Profiles for Pacific Island Agroforestry: 15-25 m tall, crown typically 30 m across
NParks Flora & Fauna Web (Singapore), Samanea saman: 20-30 m tall, crown 20-30 m
estimated: usdaZones: from its frost-free tropical range
leafRetention: semi-deciduous for a short dry spell; 0.8 is a description

entries.label: Royal poinciana / flame tree
entries.description: A wide, flat umbrella of fine ferny leaves on a short buttressed trunk; scarlet in flower, bare in the dry season.
sources: Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Delonix regia: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones (35-40 ft by 40-60 ft, zones 10B-11)
estimated: usdaZones: warm end raised to 12.5
leafRetention: deciduous in the dry season; 0.3 is a description

entries.label: Neem
entries.description: A round, fairly dense evergreen crown of drooping pinnate leaves on a straight short trunk.
sources: Orwa et al. 2009, Agroforestree Database 4.0 (World Agroforestry Centre), Azadirachta indica: height, crown, leaf dimensions (to 15, rarely 30 m; crown to 10, rarely 20 m across; leaflets 4-8 cm)
estimated: usdaZones: from its frost tolerance described (no hard frost)

entries.label: Southern magnolia
entries.description: A dense, dark evergreen pyramid rounding to an oval, branched to the ground, of large glossy leaves rusty beneath.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder, Magnolia grandiflora: height, spread, hardiness zones, habit (60-80 ft by 30-50 ft, zones 7-9)
Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Magnolia grandiflora: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones (zones 7-10A)

entries.label: Southern live oak
entries.description: A low, enormous evergreen crown, far wider than tall, on a short massive trunk and long horizontal limbs that dip toward the ground.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder, Quercus virginiana: height, spread, hardiness zones, habit (40-80 ft by 60-100 ft, zones 8-10)
Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Quercus virginiana: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones

entries.label: Camphor tree
entries.description: A broad, dense, round evergreen dome wider than tall, of glossy light green leaves on a short thick trunk.
sources: Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Cinnamomum camphora: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones (40-50 ft by 50-60 ft, zones 9B-11)

entries.label: Norfolk Island pine
entries.description: A perfectly regular, narrow cone: a straight trunk with evenly spaced whorls of level, slightly upturned branches.
sources: Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Araucaria heterophylla: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones (60-80 ft by 12-20 ft, zones 10-11)
estimated: usdaZones: warm end raised to 12.5, planted through the humid tropics

entries.label: Umbrella thorn acacia
entries.description: A flat, spreading parasol of tiny leaflets on a bare, forking trunk: the savanna tree.
sources: Orwa et al. 2009, Agroforestree Database 4.0 (World Agroforestry Centre), Acacia (Vachellia) tortilis: height, crown, leaf dimensions (4-21 m; flat-topped umbrella crown; leaflets 1-2 mm)
estimated: crownRadiusPerHeight: no spread published; 0.7 from the flat umbrella described, wider than tall
usdaZones: from its range (light frost only)
leafRetention: drops leaves in long droughts; 0.7 is a description

entries.label: Honey mesquite
entries.description: A low, open, rounded crown of drooping feathery leaves on crooked limbs from a short, often divided trunk.
sources: Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Prosopis glandulosa: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones (ST-502: 30 ft by 30 ft, rounded)
USDA NRCS Plant Guide, Honey mesquite (Prosopis glandulosa): range, leaflets
estimated: usdaZones: from its native range, Kansas to northern Mexico
leafRetention: winter-deciduous, late to leaf; months not given

entries.label: Larch
entries.description: A slender open cone of level branches with hanging twigs; a conifer whose soft needles turn gold and fall.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder, Larix decidua: height, spread, hardiness zones, habit (60-100 ft by 20-30 ft, zones 2-6)
Mitchell 1974, A Field Guide to the Trees of Britain and Northern Europe (Collins), Larix decidua: height, habit, leaf length

entries.label: Hemlock
entries.description: A soft, dense, graceful pyramid to the ground, the leader and branch tips nodding, of tiny flat needles.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder, Tsuga canadensis: height, spread, hardiness zones, habit (40-70 ft by 25-35 ft, zones 3-7)
Gilman & Watson 1993-94, US Forest Service / University of Florida IFAS fact sheet series (ST-), Tsuga canadensis: height, spread, crown shape, leaf length, hardiness zones

entries.label: Douglas fir
entries.description: A tall, sharp, regular spire on a straight trunk, lower limbs drooping, clear of branches below with age.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder, Pseudotsuga menziesii: height, spread, hardiness zones, habit (40-80 ft by 12-20 ft in cultivation, zones 4-6)
Burns & Honkala 1990, Silvics of North America vol. 1 (USDA Agriculture Handbook 654), Pseudotsuga menziesii: to 75 m and more on the coast
estimated: usdaZones: warm end raised to 9, native to the Pacific coast (Seattle 8b-9a)

entries.label: Aspen
entries.description: A slim pale trunk under a narrow, open, rounded crown of small round leaves that tremble; gold in autumn.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder, Populus tremuloides: height, spread, hardiness zones, habit (20-50 ft by 10-30 ft, zones 1-6)
Burns & Honkala 1990, Silvics of North America vol. 2, Populus tremuloides
